verification.method: scripts/verify/honduras.py reads the original UN files directly (not the site's generated data) and compares them with the built page, JSON-LD and CSV; the build itself fails if any sentence-level claim (assertClaim) stops being true; then a hand read of title, description, headline, FAQ and story text.
what: Population, rank, share, growth, density, land area; largest growth since 1950 in Latin America and the Caribbean (1 million+), about sevenfold
Third in Central America after Mexico and Guatemala; net departures every year 1950–2100; natural increase now
Life expectancy 1997, 1998, 1999 (1998 drop third-largest worldwide after South Sudan and Eritrea); deaths 1997 and 1998; 1974 dip
Births peak 2025; fertility high 1954, now, below 2.1 in 2043; third-youngest median age in the region after Guatemala and Haiti
Peak and first natural decrease 2090; urban majority 2008, urban share now and 2050; title, meta description, headline, FAQ JSON-LD, CSV rows, live counter
against: UN WPP 2024 original file WPP2024_Demographic_Indicators_Medium.csv.gz (SHA-256 286ac36b…, downloaded 2026-11-25) and interim update zip (eb7846bf…) — 75 of 75 checks match
UN WUP 2025 original file WUP2025-F15-National-Definitions_percPop_by_category.xlsx (SHA-256 5fdc43a9…, downloaded 2026-11-25); licence CC BY 3.0 IGO stated in the file
Encyclopaedia Britannica, Hurricane Mitch (read 2026-11-26): landfall in northern Honduras on 29 October 1998; more than 11,000 people killed, mostly in Honduras and Nicaragua
verification.result: All figures match. The UN series is described as counts; the hurricane's date and toll are attributed to Britannica; the 1974 dip is given without a cause.
